title: A long row of closed lockers
description: Sets up the puzzle: a row of identical closed lockers numbered from 1 to 100, and the question of which stay open.

title: The toggles of locker 12 are its factors
description: Shows that locker 12 is toggled by the people 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12, its factors, which join in three partner pairs.

title: 36 has a factor that pairs with itself
description: Shows the five factor pairs of 36, where the last pair is 6 with itself, so 36 has 9 factors, an odd number.

title: Square lockers stay open
description: Shows all 100 lockers in a 10 by 10 grid: the 10 square numbered lockers stand open and every other locker is closed.

title: An even count closes, an odd count opens
description: Before and after comparison: locker 12 is toggled 6 times and ends closed, locker 16 is toggled 5 times and ends open.

topic_name: Squares as Areas, Digits and Zeros
title: A square of side 6 has area 36
description: Shows a square of side 6 units made of 36 unit squares, so its area is 6 squared, which is 36, not 12.

topic_name: Squares as Areas, Digits and Zeros
title: Only the last digit decides
description: Shows that the last digit of 34² comes only from the last digit 4: 4² = 16 ends in 6, so 34² = 1156 ends in 6.

topic_name: Squares as Areas, Digits and Zeros
title: Squares ending in 1, and numbers that never are squares
description: Shows two squares that end in 1 because their numbers end in 1 or 9, beside five numbers ruled out as squares by their last digit.

topic_name: Squares as Areas, Digits and Zeros
title: Squaring doubles the end zeros
description: Shows 3000 × 3000 = 9000000: three zeros from each factor give six zeros at the end of the square.

topic_name: Squares as Areas, Digits and Zeros
title: Grow a square by one border
description: Shows the square builder's core move: a 4 by 4 square of 16 tiles grows to 5 by 5 by adding an L shaped border of 9 tiles.

title: Odd numbers wrap into a square
description: Shows a 6 by 6 square of dots built from inverted L shapes of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 dots, so the first 6 odd numbers add to 36.

title: Taking odd numbers from 38 leaves 2
description: Shows 38 as a bar cut into pieces of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 with 2 left over, so 38 is not a perfect square.

title: One odd strip turns 35² into 36²
description: Shows a 35 by 35 square with an L shaped strip of 71 unit squares added along two sides to make a 36 by 36 square.

title: From 125 squared to 126 squared
description: Shows that 126 squared is 125 squared plus an L shaped border of 251, the 126th odd number.

topic_name: Gaps Between Squares and Triangular Numbers
title: Ten numbers between 25 and 36
description: Shows a number line from 25 to 36 where the 10 whole numbers strictly between the two squares are marked.

topic_name: Gaps Between Squares and Triangular Numbers
title: Fewer squares in each hundred
description: Shows the number of perfect squares in each block of 100 from 1 to 1000 as columns of dots, falling from 10 to 1.

topic_name: Gaps Between Squares and Triangular Numbers
title: Two triangles fill a square
description: Shows a 5 by 5 square of dots split along a staircase into a triangle of 15 dots and a triangle of 10 dots.

topic_name: Gaps Between Squares and Triangular Numbers
title: 32 numbers between 256 and 289
description: Shows 32 whole numbers lying strictly between 16 squared and 17 squared on a number line.

topic_name: Square Roots: The Side from the Area
title: The side of a square of area 64
description: Shows a square of area 64 square cm made of 64 unit cells, with each side 8 cm, the positive square root of 64.

topic_name: Square Roots: The Side from the Area
title: List squares until you hit 576
description: Shows the squares from 20 squared to 24 squared listed in order until 576 is reached, so the square root of 576 is 24.

topic_name: Square Roots: The Side from the Area
title: Nine odd steps down from 81
description: Shows 81 reduced to 0 by subtracting 1, 3, 5, up to 17, in exactly 9 steps, so √81 = 9.

topic_name: Square Roots: The Side from the Area
title: The side of a 441 square metre square
description: Shows a square of area 441 square metres whose side is 21 metres, the square root of the area.

title: 324 splits into two equal groups
description: Shows the prime factors of 324 split into two identical groups, 2 × 3 × 3 and 2 × 3 × 3, so 324 = 18 × 18.

title: Every prime twice, or one left alone
description: Shows 1156 with every prime appearing an even number of times, so 1156 = 34², and 2800 with a single 7, so it is not a square.

title: Pair the primes of 72
description: Shows the prime tiles of 72 with two 2s and two 3s locked in pairs and one 2 left alone, so multiplying by 2 makes a square.

title: Trap the root of 1936
description: Shows the square root of 1936 trapped between 40 and 50, narrowed to 44 or 46 by the last digit, and fixed at 44 because 45 squared is too big.

title: √250 lies between 15 and 16
description: Shows √250 on a number line between 15 and 16, closer to 16, because 15² = 225 and 16² = 256.

title: The handkerchief must fit the cloth
description: Shows a square cloth of area 125 square cm with an 11 cm square fitting inside it, while a 15 cm square is far too big.

title: Trap √52 between 7 and 8
description: Shows √52 trapped in the band between 7 and 8 on a number line, since 7² = 49 and 8² = 64, so 52 is not a perfect square.

title: Four layers of 16 make 64
description: Shows a cube of edge 4 split into 4 layers of 16 unit cubes, so it holds 4 cubed, which is 64, unit cubes.

title: The five cubes with three digits
description: Shows the cubes from 64 to 1000 in a row, with the five three digit cubes 125, 216, 343, 512 and 729 highlighted.

title: Two negatives make positive, three make negative
description: Compares (−6)² = 36, which is positive, with (−6)³ = −216, which is negative.

title: Three layers of nine make 27
description: Shows a cube of edge 3 built from 3 separated layers of 3 by 3 unit cubes, 27 unit cubes in all.

title: 1729 is two cubes in two ways
description: Shows 1729 made as 1 cubed plus 12 cubed and also as 9 cubed plus 10 cubed.

title: Blocks of odd numbers make cubes
description: Shows the odd numbers in blocks of 1, 2, 3 and 4 terms, whose sums are 1³, 2³, 3³ and 4³.

title: Cube differences settle at level 3
description: Shows the cubes 1, 8, 27, 64 and 125 with their differences taken three times until they become the constant 6.

title: A cube difference beats a square difference
description: Before and after comparison on small numbers: 4³ − 3³ = 37 against 4² − 3² = 7, drawn as two bars to scale.

topic_name: Cube Roots by Grouping in Threes
title: 3375 splits into three equal groups
description: Shows the prime factors of 3375 split into three identical groups of 3 × 5, so 3375 = 15 × 15 × 15.

topic_name: Cube Roots by Grouping in Threes
title: 729 splits into three equal groups
description: Shows the six prime factors 3 of 729 split into three identical groups of 3 × 3, so 729 = 9 × 9 × 9.

topic_name: Cube Roots by Grouping in Threes
title: Complete the group of three 7s
description: Shows the cube root tripler's core move: the primes of 1323 grouped in threes, with one 7 missing, so multiplying by 7 makes a perfect cube.

topic_name: Summary: A Square and A Cube
title: Square, cube and root
description: A visual summary of three ideas: a square is an area, a cube is a volume, and a root undoes the power.

topic_name: Summary: A Square and A Cube
title: Varga, ghana and mula
description: Shows the old Indian words for a square, a cube and a root: varga, ghana and mula, the root of a plant.

topic_name: Summary: A Square and A Cube
title: Neighbours that add to squares
description: Shows the row 3, 6, 10, 15 where each pair of neighbours adds to a perfect square: 9, 16 and 25.
